evidence: The preparation of oxide layers by molecular layering is based on self-restrained chemisorption of metal halide (MCl n ) and water vapor under the conditions close to monolayer surface coverage. For instance, on a hydroxylated surface of silicon, this process can be described by the following chain of surface reactions: (Si–OH) m + MCl n (Si–O–) m MCl n m m HCl,(1) (2) Multiple repetition of reactions (1) and (2) with the intermediate removal of excess reagents and reaction products results in the formation of an oxide layer of the required thickness. Chromium oxide layers were prepared by alternately treating the surface of semiconducting plates ≡Si–O–() mMClnm– nm–() H2O+ ≡Si–O–() mM(OH)nm– nm–() HCl.+. The formation of chromium oxide nanostructures was studied using the following synthetic processes (technological schemes): (1) Alternate treatment of the surface with CrO2Cl2 and CH3OH vapors (CH3OH is a neutral hydroxylating reagent). (2) Alternate treatment of the surface with CrO2Cl2 and (CH3OH + H2O) vapors (CH3OH is a reducing hydroxylating reagent).
